overall: The AG found the Carver Board of Selectmen violated the Open Meeting Law by delaying approval and release of executive session minutes, inadequately detailing discussions, omitting document lists, and vaguely stating executive session purposes, but found no intentional violation.

allegations.summary: Board argued the complaint was not timely filed with the Board within 30 days; the AG considered whether the filing period was triggered.
allegations.key_passage: Because the 30-day filing period began to run when she received the minutes on December 27, 2011, Ms. Padovani's complaint is timely.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to respond within 10 days to a written request for executive session minutes made in an envelope handed to the Chair.
allegations.key_passage: It appears that the Board acted quickly to provide a reply once they discovered her request for executive session minutes, therefore we find that any violation was de minimis.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to create executive session minutes in a timely manner.
allegations.key_passage: While Ms. Padovani alleges that the Board failed to create executive session minutes in a timely manner, we do not find this to be the case.

allegations.summary: The Board waited nine to twelve months to approve final minutes of four executive sessions, which the AG found untimely.
allegations.key_passage: Even if the Board believed that the executive session purpose warranted continued non-disclosure, the Board was obligated to approve final minutes in a timely manner.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to release executive session minutes once the purpose for confidentiality expired after the Town Administrator contract was executed.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to release the executive session minutes once the purpose for confidentiality expired.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board did not review executive session minutes at reasonable intervals to determine whether continued non-disclosure was warranted.
allegations.key_passage: The Board should therefore have reviewed the executive session minutes at a subsequent meeting and released all four sets of minutes describing the Town Administrator contract negotiations

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the executive session minutes lacked sufficient detail; the AG found the summaries of discussions inadequate for a non-attending member of the public.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Board did not comply with the Open Meeting Law's requirement that it provide a sufficiently detailed summary of the discussion that occurred during these executive sessions.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged executive session minutes did not include copies of documents used; the AG found minutes failed to list documents referenced during sessions.
allegations.key_passage: Although we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by not including a list of documents used at meetings in its minutes

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged documents used in executive session were not provided; the AG noted it was unclear whether these were specifically requested and gave a reminder.
allegations.key_passage: We remind the Board of its obligation to provide, upon request, documents used during its meetings, except to the extent they may be withheld pursuant to G.L. c. 30A, § 22(f).

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the minutes lacked start and adjournment times for executive sessions; the AG found no violation as to executive session times.
allegations.key_passage: Public bodies are not required to provide adjournment times, nor are they required to provide start and end times for individual discussion topics, including executive sessions.

allegations.summary: AG found on its own review that the notices and open session statements gave insufficiently specific purposes for entering executive session (not raised in the complaint).
allegations.key_passage: Upon reviewing Ms. Padovani's complaint, we discovered similar deficiencies in connection with the December 20, 2010; February 25, 2011; and March 8, 2011 executive session meetings.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate.
Attend Open Meeting Law training conducted by an approved attorney or organization, or view the Attorney General's online training video, with all members certifying compliance within sixty days.
Amend the executive session minutes for December 20, 2010; February 25, 2011; March 8, 2011; and March 29, 2011 to include the missing detail, within thirty days of receipt.
Review OML 2011-56 to ensure future compliance regarding the specificity of executive session purpose statements.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution the Board that a determination by our office of similar violations in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
